quote: I was struggling
speaker_description: Taylor, 20, Georgia Pathways enrollee who studies nursing and works at a fast-food restaurant
job_statement_rewrite: When my Medicaid needs proof of work and school each month, I want to know which papers to upload and how, so I can keep my coverage.

quote: Just come when you say you’re going to come
speaker_description: Wanda Bradley, 68, retiree who is legally blind and depends on MARTA buses
location_in_source: Rider quote near top of article
job_statement_rewrite: When I cannot drive and the bus is my only way around, I want it to arrive when the schedule says, so I can plan my day.

quote: I was very anxious
speaker_description: Erin Hayes, bought a used car on a subprime loan from a buy-here-pay-here lot near Raleigh, NC
location_in_source: Her account of the car being shut off
job_statement_rewrite: When my car payment is late and the lender can switch the car off, I want a way to keep it running, so I can get home and to work.

quote: I couldn’t find anybody reliable
speaker_description: Janine Hunt-Jackson, Lockport, NY, authorized for 35 hours of home care a week
job_statement_rewrite: When my aide leaves and the hours are approved but unfilled, I want a dependable replacement, so I can stay at home safely.

quote: I was really mad.
speaker_description: Marlon Nelson, Silver Spring, MD, after his neighborhood Walgreens closed
job_statement_rewrite: When my neighborhood pharmacy closes, I want somewhere close to get vaccines and refills, so I can keep up my care.

quote: I don’t have much free time anymore.
speaker_description: Annabel Campos, 30, full-time caregiver for her mother on dialysis, West Texas
job_statement_rewrite: When my mother needs dialysis three days a week far away, I want the trips to be manageable, so I can have some of my own life.

quote: it was definitely scary
speaker_description: Meghan Maher, Florida, left a cancer-research career to care for her mother and then her father
job_statement_rewrite: When caring for my parents takes my working hours, I want flexible work that still pays, so I can care for them without losing my footing.

quote: Having to give them that much availability, it means you’re at their mercy
speaker_description: Retail worker whose husband works Monday to Friday (unnamed in excerpt)
job_statement_rewrite: When my employer needs me available most of the week, I want to know my hours early, so I can plan child care and our family's week.

quote: [The buses] are free, and that’s good, but they still don’t show up
speaker_description: Winters, Memphis bus rider who spent $130 on rideshare in three months
job_statement_rewrite: When the bus does not show, I want a backup that does not drain my budget, so I can still get where I need to go.

quote: I could barely stand when I got home.
speaker_description: Rodrigues, plasma donor who gives twice a week
job_statement_rewrite: When my wages don't cover the month, I want a fast source of cash that doesn't hurt my health, so I can get by until a second job.

quote: lifeline
speaker_description: Luis Barberena, San Antonio, sells plasma twice a week because he can't get 40 hours of work
job_statement_rewrite: When I can't get full-time hours, I want reliable extra cash each week, so I can cover what my paycheck doesn't.

quote: That’s the first time someone opened my eyes to the benefits cliff.
speaker_description: Hamad, worker weighing a raise against losing public assistance
job_statement_rewrite: When a raise would cost me more in lost benefits than it pays, I want to see the math beforehand, so I can decide whether to take it.

quote: I’ll skip a meal or wait later several hours to take a pill.
speaker_description: Vedder, home care recipient whose caregivers sometimes don't show or have shifts cut
job_statement_rewrite: When my aide's shift is cut or missed, I want someone to cover the essentials, so I can eat and take my medicine on time.

quote: is one thing that we really need here.
speaker_description: Mark Pieper, dialysis patient in Chadron, Nebraska, whose rural unit closed
location_in_source: Interview after his last local treatment
job_statement_rewrite: When the dialysis unit near me closes, I want treatment within a reasonable drive, so I can keep three sessions a week.

quote: It’s giving me anxiety, it’s making me worry and this is a daily thing.
speaker_description: Dejane Hester-Taylor, Gwinnett County, GA, borrowed about $2,700 against her car title
job_statement_rewrite: When I owe more than I borrowed on my car title, I want a way out of the loan, so I can stop worrying the car will be taken.

quote: few, if any, other options for meeting short-term liquidity needs
speaker_description: American Bankers Association and state bank associations, letter to Congress
job_statement_rewrite: When my account runs short before payday, I want the payment to go through anyway, so I can avoid a returned payment.

quote: What we are doing is working
speaker_description: Gov. Brian Kemp, on Georgia Pathways to Coverage
job_statement_rewrite: (Policy view) Tie coverage to documented work or school so enrollees stay connected to jobs.

quote: enabled customers to obtain loans who would otherwise be unable to obtain financing
speaker_description: Trevizo, auto finance representative, on starter-interrupt devices
job_statement_rewrite: When my credit is poor and I need a car, I want a lender willing to finance me, so I can drive to work.

quote: They have a tremendous hold over people
speaker_description: Van Alst, quoted by the AJC on lenders' GPS trackers and kill switches
location_in_source: Paragraph on kill switches in Georgia
job_statement_rewrite: When my car can be disabled remotely, I want clear rules on when that can happen, so I can keep getting to work.

quote: It’s barbaric
speaker_description: Dr. Miriam Atkins, Georgia oncologist whose patients have given up treatment for fear of debt
job_statement_rewrite: When I need cancer treatment I can't afford, I want care without ruinous debt, so I can finish treatment.

quote: That's just prohibitive for a lot of low-income families.
speaker_description: Adam Ruben, Economic Security Project, on the end of IRS Direct File
location_in_source: Quote on cost and time of filing
job_statement_rewrite: When I file a simple return, I want to do it free and fast, so I can keep all of my refund.

quote: eliminating access to financial services
speaker_description: Nicholas Anthony, Cato Institute, on the CFPB overdraft cap
job_statement_rewrite: (Policy view) Keep overdraft coverage available as an opt-in service rather than cap its price.

quote: RiteCheck customers told me clearly that bank fees were an important factor
speaker_description: Lisa Servon, researcher who worked as a check-casher teller, relaying customers
job_statement_rewrite: When my paycheck needs to become cash today, I want a clear, upfront fee, so I can avoid surprise bank charges.

quote: You’re left at a bus stop wondering, will this bus show up or not?
speaker_description: Jeremiah Jones, advocacy director, Propel ATL
job_statement_rewrite: When the app shows a bus that never comes, I want to know the truth, so I can choose another way in time.

quote: one of the highest overhead costs for small business owners
speaker_description: Beth Milito, NFIB Small Business Legal Center, on swipe fees
job_statement_rewrite: When customers pay by card, I want processing to cost less, so I can keep more of each sale.
